resolution.title: syncd: Skip VID-to-RID translation for FlexCounter removal
resolution.description:
Fixes sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#29260
FlexCounter removal only requires the VID, but processFlexCounterEvent currently performs VID-to-RID translation for both SET and DEL events.

When a dynamically recreated object such as PORT_SERDES is removed, its mapping may be deleted before the corresponding stop_poll event is processed. This causes a misleading missing-VID error even though the counter cleanup succeeds.

Only translate VID to RID for SET events and add a regression test ensuring DEL does not query the mapping.

### Description of PR

Summary:
Avoid false `processFlexCounterEvent` errors when removing FlexCounter entries whose SAI objects and VID-to-RID mappings have already been removed.

For `stop_poll`/`DEL`, FlexCounter removal only requires the VID. However, `Syncd::processFlexCounterEvent()` previously attempted VID-to-RID translation for both `SET` and `DEL`.

For dynamically recreated objects such as `SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_PORT_SERDES`, the old VID-to-RID mapping may legitimately be removed before the corresponding FlexCounter `DEL` event is processed. This produced misleading errors such as:
```
processFlexCounterEvent: port VID oid:0x57..., was not found
(probably port was removed/splitted) and will remove from counters now
```

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
CPO platforms may register PORT_SERDES objects with the PORT_PHY_SERDES_ATTR FlexCounter group. These objects can be removed and recreated when updated SerDes parameters are applied.
The stop_poll event for the old object may therefore be processed after its VID-to-RID mapping has been removed. Since the removal path does not use the RID, attempting the translation is unnecessary and generates a misleading error.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:N/A

#### How did you do it?
Changed Syncd::processFlexCounterEvent() so that VID-to-RID translation is performed only for SET/start_poll.
The DEL/stop_poll path now directly removes the counter using the VID.
The existing SET behavior is preserved: if its VID-to-RID translation fails, Syncd logs the error and falls back to removing the stale counter entry.
Added a unit test using a mock Redis client to verify that FlexCounter removal does not call getRidForVid().

#### How did you verify/test it?
Validated on a 64-port CPO platform running docker-syncd-brcm-rpc.
Test procedure:
1. Installed the updated syncd-rpc package.
2. Restarted the syncd container.
3. Triggered the PORT_SERDES remove/recreate workflow.
4. Observed two PORT_PHY_SERDES_ATTR start_poll events.
5. Confirmed that no new processFlexCounterEvent: port VID ... was not found errors were generated.
Result:
```
post_upgrade_flexcounter_vid_errors=0
post_upgrade_serdes_start_poll_events=2
```
The last occurrence of the target error was from before the updated syncd binary was installed.
A regression unit test was also added:
```
SyncdTest.FlexCounterRemoveDoesNotRequireVidToRidTranslation
```

#### Any platform specific information?
The issue was reproduced on a Broadcom-based CPO platform where PORT_SERDES objects participate in PORT_PHY_SERDES_ATTR FlexCounter polling.
The fix is platform-independent and applies to all dynamically removed SAI object types processed by this FlexCounter path.
